text:
alex: Quick bug report — FastAPI service intermittently stalls when we use redwood.AsyncClient as a global dependency. Errors seen: "There is no current event loop" and long tail latencies.

alex: Minimal pattern: create AsyncClient at module import, return from dependency, await client.generate inside handlers. Works then after some token refresh/backoff the worker blocks.

maria: I traced it: auth refresh sometimes falls back to a sync code path that uses requests + time.sleep on certain httpx errors. Blocking sleep in the event loop = ouch.

sam: Also hit helpers that do asyncio.run() under the hood in tests, causing "asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop" with pytest-asyncio. Two separate but related DX regressions.

jules: Priority P0. Immediate mitigations: run refresh at startup, or force async-only path via env. Long term: remove sync fallbacks from async code paths, replace time.sleep with asyncio.sleep/anyio, and provide explicit async/sync public APIs instead of hidden asyncio.run.

maria: Typing fix: AsyncClient stub should have distinct overloads so mypy/editor warn when using sync-only helpers. Also suggest init-time check: if running in event loop and transport is sync-only, warn or error.

ci-bot: Created RED-4123 and linked logs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4123 :white_check_mark:

ajules: I'll draft a patch: gate sync fallback behind opt-in flag, add AsyncClient __aenter__/__aexit__, use asyncio.sleep in backoff, add uvicorn+pytest-asyncio e2e test, and docs for recommended FastAPI startup/shutdown client lifecycle.

alex: I'll attach a small repro and CI logs to the ticket.
